title: Massive 30-Foot Waves Batter West Coast as Relentless Storm System Sweeps the US
snippet: High surf advisories stretch from Southern California to Washington state, while severe storms threaten flash flooding in southeast Texas.
content:
Communities along the West Coast are on high alert as violent 20- to 30-foot waves continue to pound the Pacific shoreline this weekend. A series of powerful storm systems has whipped up hazardous coastal conditions, stretching from Southern California all the way to the Pacific Northwest.

Dangerous Coastlines and Inland Snow

Forecasters warn that the massive breaking waves present severe risks to waterfront areas, including widespread beach erosion, coastal flooding, and unpredictable sneaker waves. High surf alerts remain active along virtually the entire West Coast corridor. The latest system pushing into the Pacific Northwest is also spreading heavy rain and mountain snow inland across Northern California, Oregon, Washington, and the Cascade Mountains.

While the surf is expected to gradually subside by Monday morning, meteorologists warn that another system will bring another round of unsettled weather to the region by early Wednesday.

Downpours and Flash Flood Threats in Texas

Farther south, severe weather is hammering the Gulf Coast. Southeast Texas is bracing for widespread rain and potential flash flooding through Sunday night. Metropolitan areas including Houston, Galveston, and Freeport are forecast to receive 1 to 2 inches of rain, with isolated downpours bringing up to 4 inches or more in some locations.

Alongside the heavy rainfall, coastal Texas is experiencing wind gusts of up to 40 mph. Local authorities have issued warnings regarding saturated ground and strong winds, which could knock down tree limbs and cause scattered power outages across the region.
